blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) confidentiality is not absolute, House prosecutor Terry Ridon of Bicol Saro party-list said Saturday, arguing that the agency itself discloses financial information to courts when seeking freeze orders. Ridon said this undermines arguments that confidentiality rules prevent AMLC records from being presented before the Senate impeachment court in Vice President Sara Duterte’s trial. He pointed out that the AMLC routinely provides information to the Court of Appeals when it seeks orders to freeze assets suspected of being linked to unlawful activities. “If the confidentiality were absolute, they wouldn’t be able to provide information to […]...
